title: The fix for a bad emulator download reached only 2 of the 8 cloud phone runs
what: On 6 Nov a phone test died on one bad emulator download, so the main phone test and the cross-role test now download it themselves, up to 3 tries. The same fix was pasted by hand into those two runs only. The release run's upgrade check, the four watch screen checks, the phone conditions test, the store pictures and the watch video still take one try, so one bad download can turn a release red. The phone set-up steps are copied by hand into every run, so they drift.
expected: Every cloud phone run gets the same set-up, including the 3 tries, from one shared place.
how_often: now and then, when Google's download fails
fix_line: Move the phone set-up, with its 3 tries, into one shared step every phone run uses

title: The app is checked on one Node version but built and phone-tested on an older one
what: The checks on every push run on Node 22, and their own note says Node 20 is past its end of life and made one AI test hang. The release build, the phone tests, the watch build and the store pictures still run on Node 20. So the app you ship is built on a different setup from the one the tests passed on, and Node 20 gets no more security fixes.
expected: One Node version, set in one place, for every run.
fix_line: Move the remaining runs to Node 22 and keep the version in one file

title: If the 'what changed' tool breaks, the phone test quietly stops testing changed screens first
what: The full phone test is meant to run the parts that use what changed first, so a failure shows up early. Every line that works out those parts swallows its own errors. If the tool breaks, the list comes back empty, that early piece is quietly skipped, and nothing on the run page says it broke. The push check that lists the same flows is also set never to fail.
expected: A broken tool shows as a warning on the run page, so you know the early check did not happen.
fix_line: Print a warning when the tool fails instead of hiding it

title: The real-phone robot check after every release shows green even when it tested nothing
what: After every release, a robot check on real phones starts by itself. Without its two keys it stops green and only says 'nothing was tested' inside the summary. With keys, 'no free quota left today', 'a phone was not available' and 'inconclusive' also end green. Only a found problem turns it red. In the run list a green tick looks like a pass.
expected: A check that tested nothing ends as skipped or with a clear warning, not a plain green tick.
fix_line: Turn the no-key, no-quota and no-phone cases into a visible warning or a skipped result

title: Two 'warning only for now' checks have stayed warning-only for weeks
what: Expo's project check was made warning-only on 16 Oct, with a note that the next step makes it fail. More than five weeks later it still never fails a push. The iPhone matching check is also warning-only while iPhone work is paused, and both iPhone runs are frozen. Warnings that never fail pile up and get ignored.
expected: Each warning-only check has a date to become a real check, or is removed.
fix_line: Make the Expo check fail on new problems, and park the iPhone checks with a restart date

title: One test file never runs, and the website gate has no test
what: The feedback inbox test sits outside the folder the release run tests, and no cloud run starts it, so it can break without anyone seeing. The website gate's code has no test file at all.
expected: Every test file is run by some cloud check, and every server piece has at least one test.
fix_line: Move the feedback inbox test into the tested folder and add a small gate test

title: A phone test that fails once and passes on a re-run leaves no trace
what: When a full phone test round goes red, the written way forward is to re-run the failed jobs. If the second try passes, the round turns green and the release gate accepts it. Nothing writes down which part failed first, so a part that fails at random is never spotted, and each random failure costs a fail-fast round of up to two hours.
expected: Every part that failed and then passed on a re-run is listed, so random failures can be found and fixed.
how_often: whenever a phone test part fails at random
fix_line: Record re-run attempts and list parts that passed only on a second try
